summary: Ernest B. Havell worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Reading School and the Royal College of Art, he served in the Indian Education Service (1885–1906) and held leadership roles at art colleges in Chennai and Calcutta.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Henry Hoenigswald, and Zellig Harris. He taught at Penn (1946–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (1964–1988).
Ernest Clerc de Landresse was a scholar in Sinology and Japanology. He studied at the École des chartes (ca. 1821–1823) and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (ca. 1823–1832).

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, he taught at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of the Arts, and curatorship at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Ernest Herbert Cooper Walsh worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trent College and University College London, he later served as a Lecturer in Bengali at Oxford (1920–1921) and in Tibetan at SOAS (ca. 1937–1941).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Bristol who studied under Flinders Petrie and John Marshall. He served as Palestine's Custodian of Antiquities (1919–1922) and explored for the Archaeological Survey of India (1926–1931).
Ernest Monnington Bowden was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his education at Malvern College (ca. 1872–1878) and Pembroke College, Cambridge (ca. 1878–1881).
Ernest Paxton Janvier was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his education at Princeton University (A.B., 1916) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania.

Ernest Philip Horrwitz was an Indologist who served as Sanskrit Professor at Trinity College Dublin (ca. 1900–1909) and Sanskrit Instructor at City College of New York (ca. 1926–1928), alongside posts at Mumbai, Rangoon, and Hunter College.

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and history. Educated at Saint-Sulpice and the Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Collège de France from 1861.

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as a professor at Brown University from 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Ernst Arbman was an Indologist and scholar of religion who earned degrees at Uppsala University studying under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Jarl Charpentier. He served as a docent at Uppsala (1922) and professor of comparative religion at Stockholm University (1937–1958).
Ernst Arthur Voretzsch was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen from ca. 1888 to 1891 and succeeded Wilhelm Solf.

Ernst Carl Büchi was an anthropologist and Indologist who studied at Zurich under Otto Schlaginhaufen and at Copenhagen. He held posts at the University of Zurich, the Anthropological Survey of India (1950–1958), and the Free University of Berlin (1966–1979).

Ernst Cassirer was a philosopher who studied at Berlin and Marburg. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Hamburg (1919–1933), the University of Gothenburg (1935–1941), and later at Yale and Columbia universities.

Ernst Cohn-Wiener worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University, he taught at Humboldt-Akademie (ca. 1909–1933) and directed the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery (ca. 1934–1939).

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian educated at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, and directed the Altes Museum (ca. 1872–1896).

Ernst Fraenkel was a linguist who studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Leipzig under Johannes Schmidt, August Leskien, and Wilhelm Schulze. He was a professor at Kiel University (1909–1936) and later lectured at the University of Hamburg (1945–1953).

Ernst Förstemann worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp, later serving as head of the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held positions at St. Virgil Salzburg, the University of Vienna, and the University for Continuing Education Krems.
